read:
Read the contents of a file in the sandbox.
Output is truncated to 10000 lines, 30KB, or 2000 characters per line (whichever is hit first).
Use offset/limit for large files. When you need the full file, continue with offset until complete.
write:
Write content to a file in the sandbox. Creates the file if it doesn't exist, overwrites if it does.
Automatically creates parent directories. Use this for new files or complete rewrites.
edit:
Edit a file in the sandbox by replacing exact text. The old_text must match exactly (including whitespace).
Use edits for multiple disjoint replacements, all matched against the original file and validated before writing. Alternatively use old_text/new_text for one replacement.
Each old_text must be nonempty and unique. Overlapping replacements are rejected. Original line endings are preserved.
Use this for precise, surgical edits. Use sandbox_read to examine files before editing.
bash:
Execute a bash command in the sandbox working directory.
Returns stdout and stderr combined. Long output keeps its first 15KB and last 15KB, and the result names a sandbox log file holding the full output.
Optionally provide a shorter timeout in seconds (default and maximum: 120).
Each call is a separate execution: shell state and background processes do not carry over. Keep work in the foreground; do not use nohup or polling shell jobs to extend a timeout.
Pages commands run with bash -c using standard Bash defaults. Enable set -e or set -o pipefail explicitly when needed, or use && to make later commands depend on earlier success. Run installs directly without piping to tail; the tool already bounds output, and tail can hide diagnostics when an install times out. After a failure, inspect what completed before retrying mutations.
patch: Apply a patch to files in the sandbox. This is a FREEFORM tool: do not wrap the patch in JSON. Use *** Begin Patch, then *** Add File: path, *** Update File: path, or *** Delete File: path, and finish with *** End Patch. In updates, prefix unchanged lines with a space, removed lines with -, and added lines with +. Use @@ or @@ followed by a function/context line between hunks; no line numbers. Updates may include *** Move to: path. Paths are relative to the working directory reported by the sandbox tools. Read files and their instructions first. Conflicts reject the complete patch. Maximum input: 64 KiB.
